author: OW
premise: A young baronet famous for never having done anything useful is informed by his solicitor that he must earn his own living for one year or forfeit his inheritance. His friends treat the condition as the most amusing scandal of the season. He accepts a post as private secretary to a cabinet minister's wife.

author: OW
premise: A respectable stockbroker receives an anonymous letter informing him that he is the rightful heir to a Portuguese marquisate. He dismisses it, then cannot stop thinking about it. His wife, who has always wished for a title, begins ordering new stationery before he has replied.
setting: A villa in Clapham and the City of London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A proud princess who has refused every suitor announces she will marry the man who can bring her something she has never seen. Kings bring jewels and wise men bring wonders. A poor shepherd boy brings her own reflection in a pool, and is thrown out of the palace.
setting: A kingdom of marble palaces beside a great forest

author: OW
premise: A celebrated hostess decides to give the most exclusive dinner of the season by inviting only people who have never met. The guests include a bishop, an actress, an explorer, and a young poet who has written a scandalous book. By the second course, everyone has discovered a secret about everyone else.
setting: A house in Grosvenor Square, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: An elderly duchess who has outlived three husbands decides to write her memoirs. Every family in society is terrified. Her nephew, who stands to inherit, is commissioned to edit the manuscript, and discovers that its most scandalous pages concern his own mother.
setting: A town house in Belgravia, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A little match-seller who has never owned anything beautiful finds a jewelled comb in the snow outside a palace. She keeps it, though she could sell it for bread. The princess who lost it searches the city, and the girl must decide whether to return it.
setting: A city of towers and snow in a northern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A penniless young Irish poet arrives in London with one good coat and a letter of introduction to a duchess who has forgotten his family entirely. He talks his way into her drawing room, and within a month is invited everywhere except the one house he most wishes to enter.

author: OW
premise: An American heiress arrives in London determined to marry a duke. She discovers that the only unmarried duke is ninety and deaf. She resolves to marry him anyway, and his heir, a penniless nephew, sets out to prevent the match by courting her himself.

author: OW
premise: A king who has never laughed offers half his kingdom to anyone who can make him smile. Jesters, poets, and philosophers fail. A small kitchen maid who has never heard of the offer drops a tray of tarts in front of him.
setting: A kingdom of gardens and fountains

author: OW
premise: A celebrated composer of drawing-room ballads announces that he will write only serious music henceforth. His publisher despairs, his admirers desert him, and the one critic who has always despised his ballads is the first to call on him.

author: OW
premise: A young lord who has always been considered the dullest man in London is mistaken for a famous conversationalist by a visiting French journalist. He finds that people laugh at everything he says. He begins to believe himself brilliant, and his friends begin to worry.
setting: A club in St James's, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A selfish merchant who has grown rich by cheating the poor is visited at midnight by a little grey bird, who offers to sing him the song of his life. He agrees, expecting flattery. The song is not flattering.
setting: A rich merchant's house in an ancient city

author: OW
premise: A woman with a past returns to London after twenty years abroad, determined to see her daughter married well. The daughter does not know her mother is alive. The mother must arrange the match from the shadows without revealing herself.

author: OW
premise: A clergyman of advanced views invites a celebrated aesthete to preach in his parish church. The aesthete accepts, and delivers a sermon on the beauty of sin. The congregation is scandalised, the bishop is outraged, and the church has never been so full.

author: OW
premise: A vain young peacock who lives in a royal garden believes himself the most beautiful creature in the world. When a plain grey bird begins to sing beneath the king's window, and the king prefers the song, the peacock must decide whether beauty is enough.
setting: A royal garden in an eastern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A young man who has always worshipped beauty falls in love with a woman of extraordinary plainness and extraordinary mind. His friends are horrified. He finds that his conversations with her are the only thing in his life that does not bore him.

author: OW
premise: An eccentric aunt who believes herself psychic holds a séance for her nephews. The spirit who appears claims to be their grandfather and demands that they each confess their sins. The nephews suspect a trick, but cannot discover who is playing it.

author: OW
premise: A young prince who has been raised in a tower and never seen the world is told on his eighteenth birthday that he may ask for one thing. He asks to see a poor man. The king, who has never seen one either, sends his ministers to search the city.
setting: A kingdom of towers and gardens

author: OW
premise: A young poet who has published a volume of decadent verse is invited to stay at a country house by a lady who admires his work. Her husband, a hunting squire, does not. Over a weekend the poet must survive the shooting, the dinners, and the husband.

author: OW
premise: A respectable family discovers that their butler is the author of a scandalous novel that has become the talk of London. They cannot dismiss him without admitting they have read it, and they cannot keep him without reading the sequel.

author: OW
premise: A golden fish in a palace fountain is granted the power of speech by a fairy. It uses its gift to tell the courtiers the truth about one another. The court is thrown into confusion, and the king must decide whether to silence the fish or to listen.
setting: A palace courtyard in a southern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A brilliant young barrister who has risen by charm and cleverness is offered a seat in Parliament by a great lady, on condition that he marry her niece. He does not love the niece. He loves the lady.

author: OW
premise: A young man who has invented an invalid friend in the country as an excuse to leave London whenever he likes receives a letter announcing that the friend has died and left him a fortune. He cannot claim it without confessing that the friend never existed.
setting: London and a village in Hertfordshire, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A beggar who sits every day at the gate of a cathedral is offered a crown by an angel, on condition that he give up his begging bowl. He refuses. The bishop, who has overheard, demands to know why.
setting: The gate of a cathedral in a medieval city

author: OW
premise: A young lady of fashion who has broken twelve engagements becomes engaged for the thirteenth time. Her fiancé is determined to be the first to reach the altar. Her mother is determined to prevent the thirteenth broken engagement for superstition's sake.

author: OW
premise: A dandy who is famous for never having been seen without a buttonhole loses his last flower on the morning of a great wedding. Every florist in London is closed. His pursuit of a single carnation leads him through the length and breadth of the city.

author: OW
premise: A poor woodcutter's daughter who weaves beautiful cloth is commanded by the queen to weave a robe that will make her the most beloved queen in the world. The girl weaves for a year, and the robe she delivers is plain grey.
setting: A cottage at the edge of a royal forest

author: OW
premise: A cynical old diplomat, retired to a house in Mayfair, entertains himself by giving his young great-nephew advice on how to succeed in society by saying the opposite of what he means. The nephew follows the advice literally, with results that astonish them both.

author: OW
premise: A lady who has always claimed to be thirty-five is confronted by her son's announcement that he is thirty. She must explain the arithmetic to his fiancée's mother, who is a mathematician.
setting: A drawing room in Belgravia, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: An emperor who collects clocks from every land commands that all the clocks in his palace must strike at the same instant. The clockmakers labour for years. When at last they succeed, the emperor discovers that he cannot bear the silence between the strokes.
setting: A palace in an eastern empire

author: OW
premise: A young wife who discovers that her husband has paid the debts of a woman with a scandalous reputation believes him unfaithful. He refuses to explain. She resolves to attend the woman's ball, to confront her rival in her own house.

author: OW
premise: A committee of earnest ladies organising a lecture on the virtues of plain living invites a celebrated aesthete to speak against them, so that he may be refuted. His lecture converts the entire committee to the cult of beauty.
setting: A lecture hall in Kensington, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A water lily in a palace pool falls in love with the moon. The frogs mock her, and the goldfish tell her she is foolish. Every night she opens her petals to the moon, and every morning she closes them in sorrow.
setting: A palace pool in a moonlit garden

author: OW
premise: A young man who has always been told that he resembles his late father discovers that his father was not the man he believed. His mother, a great lady, refuses to say who was. His search for the truth leads him through the drawing rooms of London.

author: OW
premise: A shy young curate, mistaken for a famous explorer at a society reception, is asked to describe his adventures. He invents them on the spot. By the end of the evening, he has been invited to lead an expedition to Africa.

author: OW
premise: A clockmaker in a royal city builds a clock that can stop time. The king commands that it be used to make him live forever. The clockmaker warns him of the price. The king does not listen.
setting: A clockmaker's workshop in a royal city

author: OW
premise: A celebrated actress who has retired to marry a lord is invited to perform at a charity matinée. Her husband forbids it. She accepts anyway, and society must decide whether to applaud her or cut her.
setting: A theatre and a house in Mayfair, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A young lady who has resolved to marry only a man who has never been in debt is courted by a charming young lord who owes money to every tailor in London. He resolves to pay them all within a month. His tailors, who have grown fond of his custom, resolve to prevent him.

author: OW
premise: A poor lace-maker who sells her lace at the palace gate is noticed by a vain duchess who orders a veil finer than any ever made. The lace-maker works for a year and goes blind in the making. The duchess wears the veil once and gives it away.
setting: A city of bridges in a southern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A brilliant and cynical young man who has never been in love bets his friends that he can make the coldest woman in London fall in love with him within a month. He wins the bet, and finds that he has lost something he cannot name.

author: OW
premise: A family of social climbers renting a country house for the season discover that the house comes with an elderly butler who has served six generations of its owners and refuses to recognise the new tenants. He addresses all his remarks to the portraits.

author: OW
premise: A little lame boy who lives in a cottage at the edge of a great forest is visited each night by a white stag. He follows it into the forest, and finds a city where no one is lame, no one is old, and no one is happy.
setting: A great forest in a northern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A wealthy philanthropist who has given away half his fortune is accused by a newspaper of buying his reputation. His wife, who has always found his charity tiresome, rushes to defend him, and discovers she believes in him after all.

author: OW
premise: A lady who has kept a diary of every compliment she has ever received loses it at a garden party. Every guest is terrified that their compliment will be read aloud. The young man who finds it is the only guest who never paid her one.

author: OW
premise: A young princess who has been told that she is the most beautiful girl in the world goes to the market in disguise to discover the truth. A blind woman who sells flowers tells her she sings beautifully, and the princess does not know whether to be pleased.
setting: A market in a royal city

author: OW
premise: A young man who has led a life of pleasure is told by his doctor that he has a year to live. He resolves to spend it doing good, and finds that good deeds are far more difficult than bad ones. The doctor's diagnosis proves to be mistaken.

author: OW
premise: An elderly baronet who has always claimed descent from a medieval king is presented with a genealogy showing that he is descended from the king's cook. His wife is devastated. He finds it the most interesting thing that has ever happened to him.

author: OW
premise: A shepherd finds a silver bell in a field after a storm. When he rings it, every animal on the hillside kneels. The lord of the valley demands the bell. The shepherd must decide whether to give it up, or to ring it in the lord's hall.
setting: A valley at the edge of a great plain

author: OW
premise: A married woman of fashion receives a letter from a young admirer threatening to kill himself if she does not see him. She does not take it seriously. Her husband, who opens her letters, does.

author: OW
premise: A young man who has failed at every profession decides to become a critic, on the principle that criticism requires no talent. His first review is so cruel and so brilliant that he becomes famous overnight, and every artist in London wants to be insulted by him.

author: OW
premise: A miser who lives in a tower above a town counts his gold every night by the light of a single candle. One winter evening a child knocks on his door to ask for a light for her mother's lamp. He gives it grudgingly, and finds he cannot stop thinking about the child.
setting: A tower above a town in a northern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A young heiress who has been brought up to believe that wealth is vulgar falls in love with a penniless artist, and is disappointed to learn that he wishes to be rich. She resolves to teach him the beauty of poverty. He resolves to teach her the poverty of beauty.

author: OW
premise: A dinner party is thrown into chaos when the guest of honour, a celebrated talker, arrives with nothing to say. The hostess, desperate, begins to entertain the table herself, and discovers that she is far more amusing than her guest.

author: OW
premise: A rich man's son and a poor man's son are born on the same night in the same city. A fairy grants each a gift. The rich man's son is given beauty, the poor man's son a kind heart. Twenty years later, they meet at the palace gate.

author: OW
premise: A middle-aged politician of irreproachable reputation is blackmailed by a former friend who holds a letter he wrote in his youth. His wife, who admires him as a man of perfect honour, must not learn of it.
setting: Westminster and a house in Mayfair, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A woman novelist who writes moral tales for young ladies is discovered to be the author of a scandalous French novel published under another name. Her publisher is horrified. Her readers buy both.

author: OW
premise: An old organ in a cathedral that has not been played for a hundred years begins to play by itself on Christmas Eve. The bishop forbids anyone to listen. A little choirboy who cannot sleep creeps into the cathedral to hear it.
setting: A cathedral in an old city

author: OW
premise: A young man returns from three years in Australia to find that his fiancée has married his best friend. She explains that she believed him dead. He suspects that she simply grew bored. Both explanations, he decides, are equally flattering.

author: OW
premise: An Irish gentleman who has inherited a castle in the west of Ireland invites a party of English friends to stay. The castle has no roof. He insists that this is the latest fashion.

author: OW
premise: A proud young swan who believes herself above the other birds on the royal lake refuses to share her bread with the ducks. When winter comes and the lake freezes, the ducks are the only ones who know where the open water lies.
